wikipedia#2.title: 1968: At the Summer Olympics in Mexico City, American athlete Bob Beamon (pictured) achieved a distance of 8.90 m (29.2 ft) in the long jump event, setting a world record that stood for 23 years.

wikipedia#3.title: 1967: The Soviet space probe Venera 4 became the first spacecraft to perform direct in situ analysis of the environment of another planet (Venus).

wikipedia#4.title: 1963: The first cat in space, later known as Félicette, launched aboard a French Véronique rocket.

wikipedia#5.title: 1943: Pere Areny, convicted of the murder of his brother, became the last person to be executed by Andorra.

wikipedia#6.title: 1906: The Robert Burns Memorial Statue, the first public statue erected in New Brunswick, was dedicated in Fredericton.

wikipedia#7.title: 1887: Johannes Brahms (pictured) conducted the premiere of his Double Concerto, composed for violinist Joseph Joachim and cellist Robert Hausmann.

wikipedia#8.title: 1873: Renton defeated Kilmarnock 2–0 in the opening match of the inaugural Scottish Cup.

wikipedia#9.title: 1775: American Revolutionary War: In an act of retaliation against ports that supported Patriot activities in the early stages of the war, the Royal Navy destroyed what is now Portland, Maine.

wikipedia#10.title: 1748: The War of the Austrian Succession ended with the signing of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle.

wikipedia#11.title: 1587: Filipino sailors disembarked from the Manila galleon Nuestra Señora de Buena Esperanza in what is now Morro Bay, California, the first documented instance of Asians in the Americas.

wikipedia#12.title: 1565: The first recorded naval battle between Europeans and the Japanese occurred when a flotilla of samurai attacked two Portuguese trade vessels at the Battle of Fukuda Bay in Nagasaki.

wikipedia#13.title: 1356: The most significant earthquake to have occurred in Central Europe in recorded history destroyed Basel, Switzerland.

wikipedia#14.title: 1081: Byzantine–Norman wars: Robert Guiscard led an invasion of the Byzantine Empire, capturing Dyrrhachium in present-day Albania.

wikipedia#15.title: 320: Pappus of Alexandria, one of the last great Greek mathematicians of antiquity, observed an eclipse that allowed historians to calculate the approximate dates of his life.
